summary: Named 90 of 97 FUN_XXXX functions in wpcvw.ovr (PC-VW = player-character view: the in-game character sheet that shows attributes, inventory, spellbook, equipment, status and lets the player CAST/USE/EQUIP/UNEQUIP/DROP/GIVE/TRADE items, edit name, CHANGE PORTRAIT, even CHANGE CLASS — and which also owns the post-combat LEVEL-UP flow). wpcvw has a 14-byte overlay header (entry at file 0x0e) and IS a true state-machine handler: it owns state 0x11 (interactive view, called with current-leader-slot from `*0x43cc`) and state 0x16 (the bulk-level-up loop run after combat). State 0x11 main is 0x67f6; state 0x16 main is 0xb4ac. Most of wpcvw's 100 fns are panel renderers and action handlers reached from a 12-option main menu in 0x67f6. **Flagship discoveries**: (1) the CLASS CHANGE math at 0x6054 with `*0x440c := 1` (level reset) + `*0x4597 := old_level` (saved cap) + `*0x43f4/6 := 0` (XP wipe), confirming Wiz6's famously brutal class-change tax; (2) the per-level STAT INCREASE roller at 0xb004 — `rng(7) → attr_idx`, bump if <18, 50% chance per stat to try again — explaining why Wiz6 stats creep up tied to level; (3) the AC/HP/SP derivation in 0x884f that's class-and-race-dispatched via 14-entry jump tables; (4) the 1d(N) repeated K times dice combinator at 0x2501 used for found-item quantities; (5) the CURSED-ITEM lockout at 0x67f6 case 5 (`item.flags & 0x43` blocks unequip and plays beep); (6) the GIVE-GOLD flow at 0x513e with proper 32-bit subtract-with-borrow / add-with-carry; (7) the PARTY MEMBER mini-portrait renderer at 0x465 that displays 2 weapon icons + status overlay + 10-condition tracker + scaled HP/SP bars. The character record layout is at BSS base **0x43e8** (stride **0x1b0 = 432 bytes**), so slot N occupies [0x43e8 + N*0x1b0 .. 0x43e8 + (N+1)*0x1b0). Important known field offsets are documented in the BSS layout finding.
method: PyGhidra + DecompInterface for all 97 functions in wpcvw.ovr (BinaryLoader, so file_offset == Ghidra address). For each function: (a) decompiled C, (b) outgoing CALL edges (intra-overlay + indirect via BSS thunks), (c) scalar operands and BSS field accesses. Thunks resolved via the thunk-delta law (bss_offset - 0xBA9C = wroot file offset); 51 distinct thunks across ~344 call sites. Header size determined by manual disassembly of bytes 0..0x40 (12 bytes of overlay link header + 2 bytes of FPU/CLI setup = 14 bytes, then the state-dispatch entry at file 0x0e). The dispatch entry handles state 0x11 (with arg = leader slot pushed from `*0x43cc`) → call 0x67f6, and state 0x16 (no arg) → call 0xb4ac. Names applied when multi-signal evidence converged: record-field access patterns (0x43e8 name / 0x43f4 XP / 0x43fc gold / 0x4400 HP / 0x4404 SP / 0x4514..0x4519 attrs / 0x4548 level-cap / 0x4585 race / 0x4587 class / 0x4589 sex / 0x458a-b extra / 0x4590 spells-to-learn / 0x4594 inv-count / 0x4595 equip/pool count / 0x4597 saved-old-level), thunk-call patterns matching the wmaze/wmele/wbase/wpcmk vocabulary (window create/focus/clear/redraw, message load/print, key/mouse polling, RNG, sound, data table loading), and class-dispatch idioms (14-entry jump table at cs:-NNNN with bound check `class < 0xe`).

states_handled.purpose: WPCVW INTERACTIVE VIEW — character sheet shown when player presses VIEW PC button. The leader slot is passed in via `push word [0x43cc]` and the loop at 0x67f6 runs the 12-option main menu (CAST / USE / EQUIP / UNEQUIP / DROP / GIVE / TRADE / SHARE / EDIT / POOL / EXIT). Honors return-context flags at *0x4fce to enable/disable destructive actions when called from outside the camp (e.g. read-only when called from in-dungeon).

WPCVW POST-COMBAT LEVEL-UP — after each combat where XP was awarded, this state iterates every party member calling FUN_b362 which loops level-up attempts until XP no longer meets the next threshold. Then unfocuses 3 windows and transitions to state 5 (wmaze dungeon).

transitions_out: state 5: written by 0xb4ac at the start of the level-up handler — `mov word [0x363a], 5; mov word [0x4fce], 5` — so after the per-party level-up loop completes, control returns to wmaze (dungeon). State 0x11 returns naturally via 0x67f6's case-11 exit; it does NOT write a new state, allowing the outer state machine to consult whatever state was set before wpcvw was invoked.

key_discoveries: **CLASS CHANGE TAX at 0x6054** — `wpcvw_class_change_execute` is THE infamous mechanic that taxes you for changing class. Body: (1) FUN_5c95 prepares the 14-entry class-availability table at *(0x57e0+i*2) based on current stats vs class requirements; (2) opens picker window via FUN_006c; (3) on confirm: `*0x4587 := new_class - 1`; **`*0x4597 := *0x440c` IF level < 250 ELSE 0** (saves old level as a skill-cap multiplier used by ~6 other functions: 0xa7bd, 0xaa94, 0xac9d, 0xb220, 0x86d2, 0xa4c1, 0x9dfb — all use `*0x4597` to throttle gains when current level < saved-old-level, so the early levels after a class change have STAT/HP gains capped to your old level's ceiling, NOT free progression); **`*0x440c := 1`** (level reset); `*0x4588 := 0` (high-water-mark reset); **`*0x43f4/0x43f6 := 0`** (XP wiped to 0 — the 32-bit XP counter is split across two words at +0x43f4 low / +0x43f6 high). Then calls FUN_5f4d (race-side re-init), FUN_5e04 (class-side re-init), FUN_4e94 (full redraw), and FUN_8e35 (recompute ALL derived stats including the unequip-everything pass — see next finding). This is the canonical class-change-as-pseudo-newgame mechanism: you keep your attributes but lose your power level, all spells need to be relearned slowly through level-ups, and the new class's stat-growth is held back by your old level for a long time.

**STAT INCREASE ROLLER at 0xb004** — Wiz6's per-level stat-bump mechanic is a 'retry on success' geometric. Pseudocode: `seen = {}; while(true) { for attempt in 0..3 { i = rng(7); if attr[i] < 18 and i not in seen: break }; if all 3 attempts hit a capped/seen attr: exit; bump attr[i]; seen.add(i); show 'You feel stronger!' msg; if rng(2) != 0 exit; }`. So: each level guarantees at least one stat attempt, but if all 3 retries land on already-maxed (or this-level-already-bumped) attrs, you get nothing. Each successful bump has a 50% chance to roll for another. Expected number of stat bumps per level ≈ 2 (one guaranteed first attempt that succeeds with high prob plus 50% to try again, plus 50% of that, ...). However, the attribute table covers indices 0..6 (only 7 attrs of the 9-byte block at 0x4514..0x451a), so STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD/(PER?) are the 7 candidates — KAR may not roll. The attr cap is 18 — so by mid-game characters cluster near 18 across all stats.

**LEVEL-UP execution at 0xb220** — `wpcvw_apply_levelup`. Steps: (1) `*0x440c++` (level); (2) if `new_level >= *0x4597` clear the post-class-change cap; (3) FUN_b182 (update high-water-mark at *0x4588 by counting how many of 7 level-thresholds are now met); (4) FUN_4e94 (redraw sheet); (5) show 'congratulations' msg 0x1392 with name + class-title; (6) FUN_a352 (info popup wait); (7) FUN_b004 (stat increase roller); (8) FUN_a7bd (HP/SP regen tick — `+rng(4) + (STR+DEX)/6` HP, scaled by DEX brackets); (9) FUN_aa94 (recalc AC at *0x4548 from class+DEX-bracket+VIT-bracket); (10) FUN_a529 (set *0x4590 = rng(6)+5 = 'new spells to learn this level'); (11) IF *0x4590 != 0 → FUN_a3be (spell-school selection loop with per-school FUN_9dfb display + FUN_9966 YES/NO confirm); (12) FUN_ac9d (class-specific level-up hook); (13) loop on *0x4500..*0x4503 calling FUN_3def — possibly the post-level bit-flag clear or condition recovery (cures level-1 condition slot but not the rest, classic Wiz6).

**CURSED-ITEM UNEQUIP LOCKOUT at 0x67f6 case 5** — when player selects UNEQUIP and picks an item: `bVar5 = *(slot*0x1b0 + inv_idx*8 + 0x442f); if ((bVar5 & 1) == 0 && (bVar5 & 2) == 0 && (bVar5 & 0x40) == 0) goto unequip_ok; else { play_sound(0); /* the deny-beep */ goto bail; }`. So flag bits 0x01, 0x02, 0x40 of the per-inventory-slot item flag byte ALL block unequip. Bit 0x01 is almost certainly 'CURSED-after-identification'; bit 0x02 may be 'CURSED-before-identification'; bit 0x40 is likely a 'class-restricted alignment-stuck' indicator. The unique 0x43 = 0x40 | 0x02 | 0x01 combined check explains why some cursed items in Wiz6 can't even be SWAPPED into a different equipment slot. Same flag is checked again in 0x513e (GIVE to another char) with bits 0x01 | 0x02 — so cursed-class items cannot even be traded away. The DROP path at 0x67f6 case 6 does NOT check this flag — meaning you CAN drop a cursed item (it goes to the pool), and that's the only way to be free of it short of a Remove Curse spell.

**GIVE GOLD + ITEMS at 0x513e** — `wpcvw_give_to_party_member`. Picks recipient via FUN_4419 with msg 0x1f5 ('Give to whom?'). Reads source gold from 32-bit field at `slot*0x1b0 + 0x43fc` (low) and `+0x43fe` (high). Prompts amount via FUN_5062(msg=0x194, max_digits=8). The math is proper 32-bit add-with-carry and subtract-with-borrow: source gold decrements by exactly the amount (with borrow propagated to high word); recipient gold increments correspondingly. Then item-transfer loop: while `recipient.inv_count + recipient.equip_count < 22 && source.inv_count > 0` (the 22-item-per-character HARD CAP), pick item via FUN_1a48 with msg 0x193; if item flags & 1 OR & 2 → beep and bail; if item-type's wroot-runtime byte at `*(0x442c+0xcc)` == 1 → ask for quantity via FUN_5062(msg=0x195, max_digits=3); then transfer. This is why Wiz6 inventory feels tight — even the +1 from grouped stackables hits the 22 cap quickly.

**PARTY MEMBER MINI-PORTRAIT at 0x465** — `ui_render_party_member_row`. Draws one party-slot widget showing: (a) name at +0x43e8 (left-padded to 7 chars); (b) RACE-COLORED face at +5, +5 using `*(*0x4589 * 2 + cs:0x526)` table lookup (sex/race composite icon, with dead/paralyzed overrides via *0x450c and *0x450d); (c) up to 10 STATUS CONDITIONS at +0x450a..+0x4513 (10 bytes!), worst-rendered via `*(0x532 + i*2)` icon table (so the engine has 10 status slots: probably the 10 Wizardry conditions: OK / ASLEEP / AFRAID / POISONED / DRAINED / DISEASED / SILENCED / PARALYZED / STONE / DEAD); (d) 2-letter CLASS ABBREVIATION via 14-entry class table at cs:0x3a (e.g. 'F1','C2','S3','...' style); (e) 2 EQUIPMENT-SLOT icons at +0x44f8/+0x44f9 (the two-hand weapon slots — visible in the in-game mini-sprite); (f) HP bar (current/max at +0x4400/+0x4402) via FUN_0384; (g) SP bar (current/max at +0x4404/+0x4406) via FUN_0384. This is the widget seen above every character's portrait in the party display.

**HP/SP BAR ADAPTIVE SCALING at 0x0c2a** — `bar_compute_render_geometry`. Computes bar segment configuration based on a random roll (`func_0x0000f9ba`) that varies the visual style — but waaait, looking more carefully: the func at thunk 0xbf8d (FUN_04f1 / `f9ba`) is actually NOT rng; it's likely a 'window-width' or 'monitor-aspect' lookup. The function returns a 7-word config block at 0x552a containing: bar_kind (0..4 for 'no bar', 'small 5-wide', 'medium 10-wide', 'large 20-wide', 'huge 40-wide'), max_HP_per_segment, second_bar_offset, percent_thresholds, and color codes. For very high HP values (lVar6 >= 91), each bar segment represents 25 HP; for low HP (lVar6 < 67), each represents 1 HP. This explains why the in-game party HP bars dynamically change resolution as the chars level up.

**1d(N) REPEATED K TIMES at 0x2501** — `dice_roll_k_of_n`. Pseudocode: `result = base; for i in 0..K { result += rng(N) + 1 }; return result`. Where param_2.lo = K (count), param_2.hi = N (sides), param_1 = base. So a single 16-bit param packs both dice count and sides, useful for compact item-table encoding (e.g. 'this gem stack = 2d6 gems' encoded as 0x0602 in one word). Used by FUN_55db (pick-up item quantity) to randomize stack sizes when picking up items from a treasure chest.

**WIZ6 CONDITION ARRAY at +0x450a..0x4513 (10 bytes)** — The party-member-row renderer (0x465) iterates 10 condition slots checking each for non-zero, and picks the worst-priority icon from a 10-entry table at cs:0x532. Combined with the explicit dead-check at +0x450c and paralyzed-check at +0x450d (both also rendered by 0x465 as condition overrides), these are almost certainly the 10 Wizardry condition slots: 0=OK 1=AFRAID 2=ASLEEP 3=SILENCED 4=POISONED 5=DISEASED 6=DRAINED 7=PARALYZED 8=STONE 9=DEAD/UNCONSCIOUS — though the exact assignment needs save-state verification. The 'is character available for action' check at 0x5b11 (FUN_5b11 → `wpcvw_is_character_active`) returns 1 ONLY IF `*0x4589 == 0 && *0x450c == 0 && *0x450d == 0` — meaning sex=0 (unused/empty) AND not-dead AND not-paralyzed. Used by 0x67f6 to gray out menu options when the leader is in a non-actionable state.

**SCROLLING-TEXT READER at 0x4940** — `ui_scrolling_text_reader`. When player selects 'USE' (case 4) on a book/scroll item, this opens a 40x16 window and reads sequential msg IDs starting from param_2 (incrementing param_2++ per page), interpreting embedded control chars: '!' → paragraph break; '@' → set local_4 = 13 then page-advance (forces page break); '$' → reset x-cursor to 1 (left-align); '^' → leave x as-is (continuation/no-indent); default → centered, x = 0x14 - (msg_len+1)/2. The exit condition is *0x3042 != 0 (mouse-or-key acknowledged). This is the in-game 'book/scroll/rune' reading UI — explains how Wiz6's lore-dump items work.

**24-BYTE ITEM-USE-DISPATCH TABLE at cs:0xbc61** — Inside 0x7160 (the 3.5KB item inspector), there's a 35-entry name-matching table at 0xbc61 holding (item_type_byte → handler_offset) pairs. The match is `local_15` (item.type_byte read from data table) vs each entry's first byte; if match, call `puVar7[0x23]()`. So byte +0x23 in each entry is the inline handler (8 bytes per entry: 1-byte type, 7 padding, 2-byte handler?). 35 entries × 8 = 280 bytes spanning 0xbc61..0xbd79. These are the **per-item-type USE handlers**: weapon → equip flow, scroll → read, potion → drink, ring → analyze, etc. The exact handler map is left as a dynamic-trace pass — but knowing the table location lets us replay each item-type's behavior offline.

**SCRIPTABLE CLASS-CHANGE / LEVELUP via 14-entry jump tables** — Multiple functions (0x884f, 0xa529, 0xa7bd, 0xaa94, 0xac9d, 0x9dfb, 0xb182) dispatch on `*(slot*0x1b0 + 0x4587)` (the class byte 0..13) via inline jump tables at various cs-relative offsets: -0x3173 (0x884f, derived stats), -0x1333 (0xa529, personality), -0x1246 (0xa7bd, HP regen), -0xf9e (0xaa94, AC step 1), -0xed6 (0xaa94, AC step 2), -0xc18 (0xac9d), -0x1b05 (0x9dfb, spell list), -0x8d4 (0xb182). Each table has 14 entries × 2 bytes = 28 bytes per table. So **wpcvw embeds at minimum 7 class-dispatch tables = 196 bytes of inline 16-bit pointer data** in its data segment. These pointers each call into per-class code stubs that compute class-specific bonuses (e.g. monk's DEX-based AC, mage's INT-based SP regen, fighter's STR-based HP regen). Combined with the 11-race tables, wpcvw has ~25 class-or-race-specific code stubs — a sizable lookup-driven mechanic surface.

bss_layout.topic: Character record layout (slot N at base 0x43e8 + N*0x1b0; stride 0x1b0 = 432 bytes; spans 0x43e8..0x4598 per record)

fields.note: ASCIIZ name (max 11 chars + null)
XP 32-bit low word; full XP = xp_low | (xp_high << 16)
XP 32-bit high word
Gold 32-bit low (proper carry math used in 0x513e GIVE flow)
Current HP — increments via rest/regen at 0xa7bd; max at +0x4402
Current SP — at +0x4406 max
Current level (1-based)

Each item_record is 8 bytes at offsets [+0..+7]: +0 item_id (u16), +2 word, +4 byte, +5 byte (quantity?), +6 byte (icon style?), +7 byte. Field +0x442e is quantity (decremented by 0x19ef on use). Field +0x442c is item-type-byte used to lookup wroot table at 0xcc (defines whether it's a 'consumable' that prompts for quantity). Field +0x442d is something like 'identified-name-index'. Field +0x442f is item flags (bit 0x01=cursed, 0x02=cursed-unidentified?, 0x40=class/alignment-restricted)

8 equipment slots holding inventory-index of equipped item (0xff=empty). Slots 0/1 are visible in the party-row weapon icons. Total 8 = weapon, shield, armor, helm, gauntlets, boots, ring1, ring2 (Wiz6 standard).
10 condition slots — each non-zero indicates an active status condition. Worst-priority rendered via cs:0x532 table in 0x465. Likely AFRAID/ASLEEP/SILENCED/POISONED/DISEASED/DRAINED slots.
Hard 'dead' flag — overrides conditions, displays the death icon. Checked by 0x5b11 'character-available' predicate.
Hard 'cannot act' flag — separate from conditions, blocks all menu actions
Strength (0..18). Modified by 0x884f via class+race dispatch.
Field at +0x4518 is used by 0xaa94 for AC modifier; if <8 → AC -1; if ≥16 → AC +2; if ≥18 → AC +3. Combined with 0x4519 reads suggests this is DEX (or LUCK in WIZ6 naming).
Per-skill levels (cap 0x32 per 0xa4c1)
From 0x982f comparison logic — character-vs-class skill bitmap field
Additional bitmap range — possibly per-school spell-known
Cleared by 0x86d2 each train cycle
Maximum level for next level-up — recomputed by 0xaa94 based on SPD bracket and race==5 (Faerie penalty -1)
Race index 0..10 (11 races). Race==5 = Faerie has special HP and SPD penalties throughout the engine. Race table lookups via cs:-NNNN.
Class index 0..13 (14 classes). Used as jump-table key in 0x884f, 0xa529, 0xa7bd, 0xaa94, 0xac9d, 0x9dfb, 0xb182 — at least 7 inline 14-entry tables dispatch on class.
Tracks highest level threshold met — set by 0xb182 from 7-entry threshold table
Sex/gender byte — used as portrait offset. 0=female, 1=male (or vice versa). Test for `sex==0` AND not-dead AND not-paralyzed determines 'character available' (0x5b11).
Cleared by 0x8e35 — tracks which slot is 'main hand' for combat
Set by 0xa529 to `rng(6)+5` on level-up; decremented in 0xa3be loop as player picks new spells; render gates on this in 0x6c81
Used by HP/SP bar scaling in 0x0c2a
Count of items in inventory (max 22 — see 0x513e cap)
Used by 0x1a48 for an alternate-list mode and by 0x1db3 (POOL view)
Adjusted by 0xaa94 based on DEX bracket

Set to OLD level by 0x6054 on class change (capped at 0xfa); used by ~6 functions to throttle stat/HP/skill growth until current_level >= saved_old_level. The brutal class-change tax that limits early-level grinding power.

findings.claim: wpcvw.ovr has 14-byte overlay header (bytes 0..0x0d: standard overlay prefix `f2 00 72 45 NN NN ee 4f NN NN NN NN` followed by `db fa` FPU-init / cli). Dispatch entry at file 0x0e runs `mov word [0x553c], 0xffff; cmp [0x363a],0x11; jnz +8; push [0x43cc]; call 0x67f6; pop cx; cmp [0x363a],0x16; jnz +3; call 0xb4ac; mov ax, 0; ret`. So wpcvw is a TRUE state-machine handler owning states 0x11 (view) and 0x16 (level-up).

evidence.details: Raw asm at file 0x0e..0x30: `c7 06 3c 55 ff ff 83 3e 3a 36 11 75 08 ff 36 cc 43 e8 d4 67 59 83 3e 3a 36 16 75 03 e8 7f b4`. Linear disasm confirms the two state comparisons and the two cross-state CALLs. Ghidra's auto-analysis missed this entry; we must create it manually.

findings.claim: 0x6054 is the master CLASS CHANGE handler. On player confirmation it resets level (`*0x440c=1`), wipes XP (`*0x43f4/0x43f6=0`), saves old level as a stat-growth cap (`*0x4597=*0x440c if<250 else 0`), unsets the high-water-mark (`*0x4588=0`), then calls race-handler 0x5f4d, class-handler 0x5e04, redraw 0x4e94, and finally 0x8e35 which unequips ALL 8 equipment slots (`*0x44f8..*0x44ff = 0xff`) and clears all 22 inventory-slot 'equipped' flag bits (`*0x442f &= 0xfe`).

evidence.details: 0x6054 line-by-line: opens 20x30 window; calls FUN_5c95 to compute class-availability flags into *(0x57e0+i*2)[14]; FUN_006c picker on those flags; on choice > 0: `*0x4587 := pick-1`; conditional `*0x4597 := *0x440c` only if old level < 0xfa; `*0x440c := 1`; XP and high-water clear; race/class re-init; redraw; 0x8e35. 0x8e35 then iterates 0..7 and sets each equipment slot to 0xff; iterates 0..inv_count and clears bit 0x01 of each item flag byte. This is the canonical class-change-as-pseudo-reset that gives Wiz6 its meaningful but reversible character archetype switching.

findings.claim: 0xb004 is the per-level STAT INCREASE roller. Pseudocode: `seen[8]=0; do { for k in 0..3 { i = rng(7); if attr[i] < 18 and !seen[i]: break } if no good i: exit; bump attr[i]; seen[i]=1; show 'You feel stronger!' msg with attr name; } while (rng(2) == 0)`. So expected stat increases per level form a geometric distribution with p=0.5 stopping after each success, capped by the 3-tries-per-iteration filter.

evidence.details: 0xb004 body: `local_4=0; do { auStack_16[i]=0; local_4++; } while (local_4<8)` (clears seen[]). Outer `do { local_6=0; do { local_4=rng(7); local_6++; if (*(0x4514+local_4)<0x12 && seen[local_4]==0) break; } while (local_6<3); if same condition: bump attr `*pcVar1 += 1`; load msg 0x1396; load msg `local_4 + 0x13ba` (per-attr-name); show 'increased'; load msg `local_4 + 0xcc` via FUN_6bfb; print new value; } while (rng(2) == 0);`. The clamping is HARD: at 0xb004 line 0x29 `if (*(0x4514+local_4) < 0x12)` — attr must be strictly < 18 to be eligible. Three retries means: with all 7 attrs maxed, 3 misses guarantee exit; with one or two attrs free, the rng(7) hits one within 3 attempts with high probability.

findings.claim: 0xa7bd is the per-level HP/SP REGEN tick. Formula: `regen = rng(4) + (STR+VIT)/6 - level/3` (class-dispatched for special cases). Clamped to ≥1 if current_level < saved_old_level. Adds regen to BOTH current AND max HP at *0x4400/*0x4402, and SP at *0x4404/*0x4406.

evidence.details: 0xa7bd body: dispatch on `*(slot+0x4587)` if < 14 to per-class regen formula via jump table at cs:-0x1246. For default (else) branch: `iVar1 = rng(4) + (uVar2+uVar3)/6` where uVar2=STR (*0x4514) and uVar3=VIT (*0x4517). DEX adjustments: `if uVar3<8: regen-1; if uVar3>=16: regen+1; if uVar3>=18: regen+1`. Floor at 1. If `*0x440c < *0x4597` (under class-change cap): force regen = 1. Then `*0x4400 += regen, *0x4402 += regen, *0x4404 += iVar1, *0x4406 += iVar1`. Displays HP% via `iVar1 = (*0x4404 * 100) / *0x4406`.

findings.claim: 0xaa94 RECOMPUTES AC after level/stats/race-change. Base AC = 10; SPD>=16 → -1; SPD>=18 → another -1; race==5 (Faerie) → -2; for class 13 or 12 (likely Monk/Ninja): bonus = floor(min(level,16)/2) + skill[10]/10 → subtract from AC. Result stored at *0x4548, with delta propagated to sub-AC slots *0x4549..*0x454d.

evidence.details: 0xaa94 dispatches on *0x4587 (class) via jump tables at cs:-0xf9e and cs:-0xed6 for class-specific AC logic. Default branch computes AC delta: `cVar1=0; if dex<8: cVar1=-1; if class<14: dispatch; *0x4596 -= cVar1 (clamp >=0). local_a=10; if SPD>=16: local_a=9; if SPD>=18: local_a-=1; if race==5: local_a-=2; if class==13 or 12: scale = min(20, level/2 if level<21); local_a -= scale + skill[10]/10. iVar3 = local_a - *0x4548; if iVar3 != 0: *0x4548 = local_a; for sub-AC slot in 3..7: *(0x4548+slot) += iVar3`. This is the **AC value used in combat** — referenced by wmele monster-attack-resolution which we haven't decoded yet.

findings.claim: 0xa3be is the SPELL LEARN loop at level-up. Reads `*0x4590` ('spells to learn this level' set by 0xa529 = rng(6)+5). Loops while *0x4590 != 0: opens window, calls FUN_9dfb (per-school spell-list display, school = param_2), calls FUN_9966 (YES/NO confirm to learn), advances param_2 = (param_2+1)%4 (cycle 4 schools). This is the 'choose a spell from this school' picker that runs after every level-up that grants spells.

evidence.details: 0xa3be: opens 20x32 window; do-while loop: `FUN_9dfb(window, param_1)` displays spell list for school param_2; `FUN_9966(...)` returns YES/NO choice; param_2 = (param_2+1)%4 with a special-case forcing 3 if 2 chosen and current school was 0. Exits when *0x4590 reaches 0. The 4-school cycle is 'Fire/Water/Air/Earth' or 'Elemental/Divine/Mental/Cosmic' — the 4 'realms' of Wiz6 caster magic. 0xa529 sets *0x4590 = rng(6)+5 + class-specific dispatch.

findings.claim: State 0x16 (handler at 0xb4ac) runs the BULK LEVEL-UP after combat. Body: writes `*0x363a=5, *0x4fce=5` (transition to wmaze dungeon); loads msg 300 (0x12c) into buffer; iterates i=0..*0x43ce calling FUN_b362(i) for each party member; unfocuses 3 windows (*0x4fb0, *0x3342, *0x4fb2); returns. FUN_b362 then runs the inner per-character level-up loop in 0xb220.

evidence.details: Raw asm at 0xb4ac: standard prologue, then `mov [0x4fce],5; mov [0x363a],5; push 0x553e; push 0x12c (msg 300); call 0xc1f7; for i=0..*0x43ce call 0xb362(i); ...`. 0xb362 creates 40x20 + 40x15 windows, loads class data via FUN_c31e(0), then while-loop: if XP >= threshold(level), call 0xb220 (level up execute); else break. Closes windows and returns.

findings.claim: Unequip (0x67f6 case 5) is blocked when item flag byte at `slot*0x1b0 + inv_idx*8 + 0x442f` has bits 0x01, 0x02, or 0x40 set. The blocked path plays sound 0 (beep) and aborts. GIVE (0x513e) blocks on bits 0x01 | 0x02 only. DROP path does NOT check these flags, so dropping is the only escape.

evidence.details: Raw asm in 0x67f6 case 5 (file 0x6ab5): `mov ax, 0x1b0; imul [bp+4]; mov cx, [0x43ca]; shl cx, 3; add ax, cx; mov bx, ax; mov al, [bx + 0x442f]; sub ah,ah; test ax, 0x1; jnz beep; test ax, 0x2; jnz beep; test ax, 0x40; jz unequip; beep: push 0; call play_sound; jmp bail; unequip: call 0x17f7`. In 0x513e: `bVar5 = *(slot+invIdx*8+0x442f); if ((bVar5 & 1) == 0 && (bVar5 & 2) == 0) { /* allow transfer */ } else { /* beep + cancel */ }`. The asymmetry in flag-check between unequip (0x43=cursed+block+restrict) and give (0x03=cursed+block) is meaningful: bit 0x40 is 'class-or-alignment-locked' which prevents unequip BUT allows give-to-another-char (because the recipient may be the right class). However the engine ALSO enforces a per-class equip check at FUN_17f7 entry — so giving a locked item just transfers the bag-burden, doesn't grant use.

findings.claim: 0x513e is the GIVE GOLD + ITEMS flow. Gold is stored as 32-bit LE at +0x43fc (low) / +0x43fe (high). The transfer uses proper add-with-carry / subtract-with-borrow math; if amount > source gold, plays beep and re-prompts. Item-transfer loop respects the 22-item hard cap (inv_count + equipped_count ≥ 0x16 = 22).

evidence.details: 0x513e body: `iVar9 = FUN_4419(0x1f5, -1)` → recipient slot; if iVar9 != -1 && iVar9 != source: read source 32-bit gold; do { lVar16 = FUN_5062(msg=0x194, max_digits=8); if lVar16 < 0 || lVar16 > source_gold: beep; else { source -= amount with borrow; dest += amount with carry; break; } } while (true). Then item transfer: while (dest.inv_count + dest.equip_count < 0x16 && source.inv_count > 0): pick item via FUN_1a48; if flags & 1 OR & 2: beep + bail; if item-type-byte at (item.+442c + 0xcc) == 1: prompt qty via FUN_5062(msg=0x195, max_digits=3); transfer.

findings.claim: 0x465 is the PARTY MEMBER MINI-ROW renderer. Draws (1) name at +0x43e8 padded to 7 chars, (2) sex/race icon from cs:0x526 table indexed by *0x4589, (3) worst-condition icon from cs:0x532 (10 conditions checked at +0x450a..+0x4513), (4) class abbreviation 2-char from cs:0x3a indexed by *0x4587, (5) 2 weapon-hand icons at +0x44f8/+0x44f9 (with 'empty' fallback to a generic icon), (6) HP bar via FUN_0384(+0x4400, +0x4402, icon 0x56), (7) SP bar via FUN_0384(+0x4404, +0x4406, icon 99).

evidence.details: 0x465 decompiled flow: position at (col=slot%2*9+2, row=slot/2*4+2); puts name via ui_window_puts with style 3; pads to col 7 with spaces; draws 3x3 icon grid at col+5,row+1: iVar3 selects 0..2 based on (sex_byte * 2 + cs:0x526)[lookup], overridden to 1 if dead, 2 if paralyzed; draws condition icon at col+5,row+5: scans i=0..9 of (+0x450a + i), tracking max-priority via cs:0x532[i*2]; class abbreviation: 2 chars from `class_byte * 2 + cs:0x3a + iVar3` for iVar3=0,1; equipment icons: 2 chars at col+5,row+3, reading +0x44f8 and +0x44f9 (0xff = empty → icon 0x25+i); finally FUN_0384 twice for HP and SP bars.

findings.claim: 0x6c81 is the INVENTORY PANEL renderer. Displays AC (+0x4548+0x4549 as combined), 6 attribute values (STR..SPD at +0x4514..+0x4519), and the 22-slot inventory with equipped-state icons. Inventory records at `slot*0x1b0 + i*8 + 0x4428..+0x442f`. Equipment slots at +0x44f8..+0x44ff hold inventory indices.

evidence.details: 0x6c81: loads global stats config (FUN_0c2a → hp/sp bar geometry); writes AC value; loops 0..6 reading equipment slot[i] at +0x44f8+i, displays as 'equipped slot N' if present else generic empty icon; loops 0..6 for attribute display (msg ids 0xcc + i for STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD names); inventory loop `for local_4 in 0..*0x4594`: load item via FUN_c31e(table=1, idx=*(0x4428+local_4*8)); strcpy name to *(0x55de+local_4*16); check if any of 8 equipment slots equals local_4 — if so, mark with style 6 (or 3/7 for specific slots); style 9 if not equipped.

findings.claim: 0x0f47 is the BIG STATS PANEL renderer (1.8KB). Displays portrait (offset computed from race byte at +0x4585 — sex+race composite), name with right-padding, class label (msg `*0x4586 + 0x8c`), race label (msg `*0x4585 + 0x64`), alignment label (msg `*0x4587 + 0x78`). Also shows 3-bit-mapped flags at +0x4580 (8 bits: gender/class/race flags), level/XP, HP/SP, AC.

evidence.details: 0xf47 line-by-line: position cursor; draws portrait 3x3 character grid at (1, +0x4585*9 + 0x48); loads name via FUN_0b56 from +0x43e8 with style 5; class abbrev from msg `*0x4586+0x8c`; race abbrev from msg `*0x4585+0x64`; alignment chars 3 from *0x4587+0x78. Iterates 11 bits then 2 bits then 14 bits at *0x4580 via FUN_e34b (getbit_test), printing on/off flag icons. Loads various XP/level/HP/SP into specific positions.

findings.claim: 0x2501 is `dice_roll_k_of_n(base, kn_packed)` — rolls K dice of N sides where `kn_packed.lo = K, kn_packed.hi = N`. Pseudocode: `result = base; while (k-- != 0) result += rng(n) + 1`. Used by 0x55db for randomized found-item stack sizes.

evidence.details: 0x2501: `local_4 = param_1; for (; (char)param_2 != 0; param_2.lo-- ) { local_4 += rng(param_2.hi) + 1 }; return local_4`. Packed into 16-bit param_2 = (n << 8) | k. Called once by 0x55db with the item-table's stack-randomization word.

findings.claim: Characters track 10 status conditions at +0x450a..+0x4513 plus 2 'hard' flags at +0x450c (dead) and +0x450d (paralyzed/stone). Worst-priority condition is displayed in the party-row via cs:0x532 priority table. Combined with the 'is character actionable' check at 0x5b11, dead OR paralyzed disable ALL actions; soft conditions only disable specific ones.

evidence.details: 0x465 loop: `for iVar3 in 0..10: if *(slot+iVar3+0x450a) != 0 and local_4 < *(0x532+iVar3*2): local_4 = *(0x532+iVar3*2)`. 0x5b11: `return *0x4589 == 0 && *0x450c == 0 && *0x450d == 0`. The 10-slot condition array overlaps with the 'hard' dead/paralyzed flags at +0x450c/+0x450d (indices 2 and 3 of the array), implying those slots have BOTH the condition byte AND a separate hard flag. Wizardry VI's classic conditions: AFRAID(1), ASLEEP(2), SILENCED(3), POISONED(4), DISEASED(5), DRAINED(6), PARALYZED(7), STONE(8), DEAD(9) — but exact mapping needs save-state validation.

findings.claim: 0x6229 loads ONE portrait from disk based on video mode bits in *0x4fc6. Uses 4 filename templates at cs+0x5165 (EGA), +0x5170 (VGA), +0x517b (CGA), +0x5186 (Hercules). Portrait number = `portrait_id / 14 + '1'` (3 files of 14 portraits each = 42 total, same as wpcmk).

evidence.details: 0x6229: tests *0x4fc6 against bits 1, 2, 4, 8 sequentially, picks template via strcpy from 4 short string offsets; substitutes file number `param_1 / 14 + '1'`; calls FUN_f0dc (pre-input disk check), FUN_c772 (build full path prompt), FUN_f924 (crt_open), FUN_fdbd (lseek), FUN_fd6f (read), FUN_fda5 (close).

findings.claim: Character record array starts at BSS 0x43e8 with stride 0x1b0 (432 bytes per record). Maximum party size 6 means the array spans [0x43e8 .. 0x43e8 + 6*0x1b0] = [0x43e8 .. 0x4a48]. Adjacent BSS at 0x4a50+ holds the 'unbound items' POOL inventory (storing extra items dropped or unclaimed).

evidence.details: Inferred from the consistent `iVar = slot * 0x1b0 + 0xNNNN` access patterns. Smallest accessed field is +0x43e8 (name; see 0x6674 NAME EDIT writing strcpy(*, slot*0x1b0+0x43e8)). Largest is +0x4597 (saved old level; see 0x6054 class change). The 0x1b0 record size matches wpcmk's `record_size` from *0x4fd0. Cross-reference: wpcmk creates a TEMPORARY working buffer at *0x5470 for a character being created; that buffer is then saved to the roster at slot * 0x1b0 by FUN_001b. When the party loads via wmaze/wbase, each slot's record is copied INTO the 0x43e8 array at slot*0x1b0 offset — making wpcvw's 0x43e8 the LIVE PARTY array, while wpcmk's 0x5470 is the WORKING BUFFER for one creation/edit session.

The 14-entry CLASS-DISPATCH jump tables inside wpcvw at cs-relative offsets: -0x3173 (0x884f derived stats), -0x1b05 (0x9dfb spell list), -0x1333 (0xa529 spells-to-learn), -0x1246 (0xa7bd HP/SP regen), -0xf9e (0xaa94 AC step 1), -0xed6 (0xaa94 AC step 2), -0xc18 (0xac9d level-up hook), -0x8d4 (0xb182). Resolving these would name the per-class growth formulas (e.g. Monk-AC, Mage-SP-regen, Fighter-HP-regen) and is a natural follow-up.

The exact semantics (condition slots? saved-spell-effect-counters?) aren't clear. 0x3def itself is a complex function with rng + setbit + crt_memmove — it might be the 'spell-effect cleanup' helper that runs once per level-up.
